summary: Contestants research and analyze economic trends related to the gig economy and income stability, write a research paper, and present their findings to judges. The event requires both a written submission and an oral presentation, focusing on evidence-based solutions and economic analysis. Participants must follow specific formatting, citation, and copyright guidelines.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes setup time
No more than seven (7) minutes presentation time
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
submission_requirements: Submit one combined PDF file containing Research Paper, Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form
Follow the Report format located in the Style & Reference Manual (no Title Page required)
Header information on the first page: Contestant ID Number, Harvey Rosen (Recipient’s Name), Financial Services Department (Recipient’s Department), Current Date
Document length limited to seven double-spaced, single-sided, numbered pages with one-inch margins (Works Cited not included in limit; graphs, tables, and charts are included)
In-text citations required throughout the paper
Materials must follow BPA Graphic Standards and proper use of BPA logo and/or organization’s name
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
what_to_bring: One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for presentation
competencies: Apply foundational economic concepts to analyze and interpret global and domestic economic trends
Conduct rigorous economic research using credible sources and communicate findings clearly and professionally through oral presentations and written reports
Analyze workplace economic factors such as productivity, labor markets, and technological change to inform organizational strategy and decision-making
Compare and contrast global economic systems, evaluating their effectiveness in addressing contemporary economic challenges
Evaluate strategies for promoting sustainable economic growth and apply modern metrics to measure economic performance
Utilize diverse research methodologies and digital resources to gather, analyze, and interpret economic data, ensuring ethical standards and data integrity
Critically analyze economic issues using quantitative and qualitative methods and propose evidence-based solutions aligned with industry trends

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

Contestant submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing their Research Paper and Works Cited in the correct format according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s) and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Exhibits deep understanding, explaining complex ideas clearly with insightful examples and thorough coverage.
The argument is well-organized, with smooth transitions and thoroughly expanded points, demonstrating clear reasoning.
The introduction and summary are compelling, with strong evidence and a concise, impactful summary.
The response is highly original and inventive, with well-integrated resources adding depth and creativity.
Contains very few or no grammar or spelling errors.

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Contestant maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation flows logically, with a clear and well-integrated structure. The speaker transitions smoothly between points, enhancing the overall coherence and impact.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes, and the presentation lasted no more than seven (7) minutes.

judging_notes: Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestant within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
Business Professionals of America assumes no responsibility for hardware/software provided by the contestant
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
Presentation will be stopped at seven (7) minutes
eligibility_notes: Contestants must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
